Every year in autumn the supplier receives the “harvest” of the season from its goodeid breeders. Because of the extraordinarily long and mild summer, this year it was the end of October. Goodeids do very well in long-term breeding if they are temporarily kept and bred under outdoor conditions. However, they have to overwinter indoors.

The Goodeid friends are very meticulous about keeping the locality populations pure. The fish belong to the old strain (Rio Teuchitlán).

Skiffia francesae, the Golden Skiffia, is a beautiful fish that was already considered extinct in the wild in 1978, when it was scientifically described. In 2007 a previously unknown population was discovered, but its habitat had also dried up completely in the meantime. Dedicated aquarists have managed to keep this fish in the aquarium for over 45 years now. Fortunately the trade in the animals is not subject to any restrictions, otherwise it would be feared that they would become extinct in the aquarium too because of bureaucratic hurdles.

Skiffia francesae should not be kept together with the closely related species S. multipunctata, because the two species can interbreed.
